forecast_provider: Project model, not a NASA prediction
brief_favorable_conditions: Not in the brief (replaces the pika/rabbit row). Forest of Christmas Island.
why_these_variables: General forest-climate indicators. Its extinction is attributed to introduced predators, not climate.

variables.label: Average monthly maximum temperature
variables.aggregation: Annual mean of each month's hottest-day temperature

variables.label: Dry-season rainfall
variables.aggregation: Annual rainfall sum over reference months [7, 8, 9, 10]; months selected using only 1981–2014, fixed for all locations.

t2m_max_mean.model_description: Average of (a) the mean of six simple forecasts (persistence, historical mean, recent mean, linear trend, Theil-Sen trend, autoregressive ridge) and (b) a global LightGBM model trained on every NASA series up to the cutoff year. Dry-season rainfall uses (a) only.
t2m_max_mean.interval_note: 80% band from pooled, standardized out-of-sample errors of the combined forecast (all distinct series, same horizon, only years up to the training cutoff).
t2m_max_mean.summary_text: Average monthly maximum temperature in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 28.5 °C (80% band for 2030: 28.0–29.1 °C; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 28.1 °C (+0.43 °C).

rh2m_mean.model_description: Average of (a) the mean of six simple forecasts (persistence, historical mean, recent mean, linear trend, Theil-Sen trend, autoregressive ridge) and (b) a global LightGBM model trained on every NASA series up to the cutoff year. Dry-season rainfall uses (a) only.
rh2m_mean.interval_note: 80% band from pooled, standardized out-of-sample errors of the combined forecast (all distinct series, same horizon, only years up to the training cutoff).
rh2m_mean.summary_text: Mean relative humidity in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 79.7 % (80% band for 2030: 78.7–80.8 %; coverage is not guaranteed), above the 1991–2020 average of 79.2 % (+0.51 %).

precip_dry_season.model_description: Mean of six simple forecasts (LightGBM is not used: the dry months were only defined in 2014).
precip_dry_season.interval_note: 80% band from pooled, standardized out-of-sample errors of the combined forecast (all distinct series, same horizon, only years up to the training cutoff).
precip_dry_season.data_caution: Reanalysis rainfall is the least reliable NASA POWER variable. Several sites show large multi-year shifts (e.g. Bramble Cay 2015–2025 about 42 % drier than 1981–2014; Monteverde dry-season rain about 3 times higher in 2009–2025 than in 1981–2008). A change-point test places these shifts in different years (1998–2015), so they do not point to a single data-source switch, but they may still be partly artificial. Rainfall forecasts that extend such shifts are uncertain: show the 80 % range and verify against local rain gauges before presenting them as fact.
precip_dry_season.summary_text: Dry-season rainfall in 2026–2030 is forecast to average 134.5 mm (80% band for 2030: 0.00–331.8 mm; coverage is not guaranteed), about the same as the 1991–2020 average of 134.7 mm.
